conventions.run: ${run} is ONE per-run prefix shared by every case in a run (TS: `e2e_${Date.now().toString(36)}`). Run cases in listed order: a few read state an earlier case created (see each case's `note`).
conventions.substitution: ${run}/${var} are substituted in every string of `args` and `expect` (including object keys and `path`). A string that is EXACTLY "${var}", "${var}+N" or "${var}-N" is replaced by the saved value itself, keeping its JSON type (numbers: arithmetic applied), e.g. {"index": "${len}-1"} sends a number.
conventions.path: Dot-separated. Object segment = key; numeric segment = array index (negative counts from the end, -1 = last); segment `length` = element count of an array, character count of a string, or key count of an object.
conventions.output: Output = JSON-RPC result.output; missing/undefined output is treated as null. Every op except `error`, `any` and `okOrErrorMatches` also fails if the call returned an error.
conventions.save: `save` stores the (path-selected) output; it is only stored when the expectation passes.

ops.contains: value: string → output string contains it as substring; output array → contains an element equal (deep JSON equality) to value.
ops.containsWhere: key, value: output is an array with at least one object whose field `key` equals `value`.
ops.notContainsWhere: key, value: output is an array with no object whose field `key` equals `value`.
ops.isSorted: output is an array of strings in non-decreasing order (compare by Unicode code point, same as Rust String Ord).
ops.okOrErrorMatches: pattern: the call succeeds, or fails with an error message matching `pattern` (regex, case-insensitive).
ops.any: ignore the result entirely, success or error (fire-and-forget step).
